learning_outcomes.text: The course provides the basic knowledge needed to understand the operation of optical telecommunications networks. It explores aspects relating to terminals, nodes, and transport and access infrastructures, with a focus on emerging technologies.
Students will be able to recognize the main characteristics of an optical network and solve simple problems related to its sizing.
They will be able to perform simple calculations related to quality of service.
They will acquire the skills to identify the most suitable techniques and materials to guarantee a certain service.
independent judgment (the ability to choose between different technological solutions)
communication skills (the use of appropriate technical language when presenting)
learning skills (the ability to keep up to date with emerging standards and technologies)

syllabus_topics: Optical Components Couplers, Isolators, Circulators, Multiplexers, Filters, Amplifiers, Transmitters, Detectors, Converters, Switches
Transmission Systems Crosstalk and Chromatic dispersion
Networks and Protocols SONET/SDH, OTN + GFP, Ethernet and IP
Guided tour of the GARR network node (PoP AN00-MonteDago), located at the Faculty of Engineering
assessment_rules: Student learning is assessed through an oral exam. The final grade is awarded on a scale of 30; the exam is considered passed if the grade is 18 or higher. Honors may be awarded to students who achieve the maximum grade of 30/30 and demonstrate the ability to independently apply the knowledge and skills acquired.
bibliography: Optical Networks: A Practical Perspective - R. Ramaswami, K. N. Sivarajan, G. H. Sasaki. - Third Edition - Morgan Kaufmann Publishers - 2010 - ISBN: 978-0-12-374092-2
Slides and teacher's notes are available on the Moodle platform at https://learn.univpm.it
